s1.syndrome_frame: oral pain and bleeding with radiographic evidence of bone and tooth resorption
salient_findings: cervical areas of rarefaction on periapical radiographs
radiolucent resorptive lesions on cone-beam computed tomography
key_facts: periapical radiographs showed cervical areas of rarefaction
endodontic evaluation was normal for both central incisors
5 mm probing depth on palatal aspects of both teeth
cone-beam computed tomography demonstrated radiolucent resorptive lesions
lesions originated from external palatal surface and perforated into pulp space

raw.syndrome_frame: oral pain and bleeding with radiographic evidence of bone and tooth resorption
salient_findings: cervical areas of rarefaction on periapical radiographs
radiolucent resorptive lesions on cone-beam computed tomography
key_facts: periapical radiographs showed cervical areas of rarefaction

5 mm probing depth on palatal aspects of both teeth

shortlist.label: External Cervical Resorption
shortlist.why_kept: radiolucent resorptive lesions on cone-beam computed tomography

shortlist.label: Chronic Periodontitis
shortlist.why_kept: generalized bleeding on probing and clinical attachment loss

shortlist.label: Asymptomatic Irreversible Pulpitis
shortlist.why_kept: normal response to cold testing and asymptomatic to percussion

shortlist.label: Internal Cervical Resorption
shortlist.why_kept: possibility of resorptive process affecting the tooth

shortlist.label: Periodontal Abscess
shortlist.why_kept: generalized bleeding on probing and deep probing depth

raw.rationale: The cone-beam computed tomography demonstrated radiolucent resorptive lesions cervically on the palatal aspects of teeth, which originated from the external palatal surface and perforated into the pulp space, consistent with external cervical resorption.

rejected.label: Chronic Periodontitis
rejected.why: While the patient has stage II, grade II periodontitis, the key finding of radiolucent resorptive lesions on the external palatal surface is more specific to external cervical resorption.

rejected.label: Asymptomatic Irreversible Pulpitis
rejected.why: The endodontic evaluation was normal for both central incisors, with normal response to cold testing and no symptoms to percussion and palpation, which does not support a diagnosis of asymptomatic irreversible pulpitis as the primary issue.

rejected.label: Internal Cervical Resorption
rejected.why: The resorptive lesions originated from the external palatal surface, not from within the tooth, which rules out internal cervical resorption.

rejected.label: Periodontal Abscess
rejected.why: There is no mention of a localized purulent infection within the periodontal tissues, which is characteristic of a periodontal abscess.
